lines: # Adaptive rejection sampling (Gilks & Wild, 1992), using only base R.
#   y <- ars(1000, dexp, domain = c(0, Inf), rate = 2)
#   test()  # prints PASS/FAIL and writes normal_samples.txt
# The density must be positive and log-concave on the interior of domain.
# A density need not be normalized. Supply log = TRUE for a log-density,
# especially when ordinary densities underflow. Functions and expressions
# must return one numeric value per input x; expressions use the variable x
# and are evaluated in the caller's environment. Extra arguments in ... are
# passed to the density (or bound as variables for an expression).
# initial supplies at least two distinct interior support points. If omitted,
# three default points are used, with outward expansion to bracket the mode
# on unbounded domains. For unusual location/scale, provide initial explicitly.
# dlogdensity optionally supplies a vectorized derivative of the LOG density;
# otherwise a five-point numerical derivative is used. With numerical
# derivatives, envelope validity is subject to floating-point accuracy.
# max_points caps stored tangents (sampling then uses the existing envelope);
# max_iterations limits proposals, and errors rather than returning a short run.
# Log-concavity checks cover evaluated points, derivative ordering, secants,
# and the upper/lower hull inequalities. No finite set of evaluations can
# certify global log-concavity of an arbitrary user function. Users remain
# responsible for specifying a log-concave target and its full support.

# Log integral of exp(height + slope * (x - anchor)) on [left, right].
# Endpoint-based formulas avoid exponentiating large tangent heights.

# Parallel tangents to an affine portion are the same line, to tolerance.

.ars_stop('Could not find integrable envelope tails; check density/domain and supply initial points.')
